title: Biliopancreatic Diversion Procedure in Mice
author: Vance L. Albaugh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zb4f2qw

steps.title: Preoperative Animal Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the mice for surgery by managing housing, nutrition, and immobilization.

substeps.instruction: Singly-house all animals.
Remove all bedding from cages.
Administer Ensure 12 hours before surgery.
Administer preoperative pain medication: Ketoprofen (5 mg/kg).
Ensure adequacy of anesthesia.
Place mouse on a surgical board/field over a warm water circulating blanket and immobilize gently.
Prep and drape the animal sterilely.

steps.title: Perform Midline Laparotomy
steps.instruction: Access the abdominal cavity using a midline incision.

substeps.instruction: Make a midline laparotomy incision with sharp surgical scissors, staying on the linea alba and away from the rectus abdominus muscles.

steps.title: Locate and Ligate Stomach
steps.instruction: Expose the stomach and restrict flow at the pylorus.

substeps.instruction: Gently sweep intestinal contents using cotton swabs until the stomach is located.
Ligate the stomach at the level of the pylorus with a 6-0 silk suture to impede flow without strangulating the tissue.

steps.title: Transect and Close Jejunum
steps.instruction: Isolate and divide a section of the jejunum.

substeps.instruction: Identify a portion of jejunum approximately 4cm distal to the Ligament of Treitz.
Transect the bowel using 8-0 nylon suture.
Divide the mesentery as necessary to allow sufficient mobilization and prevent torsion.
Close the proximal and distal ends of the small bowel with 8-0 nylon suture.

steps.title: Create Gastroenterostomy
steps.instruction: Establish a connection between the small bowel and the stomach.

substeps.instruction: Measure 12cm distally from the distal sutured end of the small bowel.

On the proximal end of the small bowel limb, create a running-continuous, side-to-side gastroenterostomy (at least 1.5cm in length) on the anterior surface of the stomach, just proximal to the greater curvature, using 7-0 PDS II.
Place ligatures on stomach or mesenteric vessels using 7-0 PDS II as needed for hemostasis, ensuring the blood supply to the anastomosis is not disrupted.
Once the proximal end is complete and hemostasis is adequate, create a side-to-side enteroenterostomy between the native jejunum and the gastric limb of the transposed bowel.

steps.title: Close Abdominal Cavity
steps.instruction: Clean the cavity and perform a two-layer closure.

substeps.instruction: Irrigate the abdominal cavity as necessary to remove blood clots or small bowel contamination.
Close the muscle layer using a simple, interrupted fashion with 6-0 monocryl suture, suturing the connective tissue rather than the muscle proper.
Close the skin layer using a simple, interrupted fashion with 7-0 Prolene suture.

steps.title: Immediate Postoperative Care
steps.instruction: Provide initial recovery support and hydration.

substeps.instruction: Administer 1.0 ml of warmed, sterile saline before placing mice in recovery cages.

steps.title: Postoperative Monitoring and Maintenance
steps.instruction: Manage the animals' recovery environment, diet, and pain.

substeps.instruction: Keep cages partially on a veterinary-approved heating pad for 5 to 7 days postoperatively.
Maintain mice on an Ensure diet for 24 hours post-surgery with no bedding in the cage.
Administer Ketoprofen (5 mg/kg) post-op and again at 24 hours postoperative (additional medication as needed).
Monitor general behavior (bright/alert/responsive vs. depressed/obtunded) until recovered, typically 7-14 days.
